Open a table

Source: R/open.R
lake_open.Rd

lake_open() builds a snapshot of a Delta Lake table: one version of it, replayed from the table's own log as the Delta protocol prescribes. A snapshot never changes; lake_load() builds another one of the same table, at another version or at the version the log now ends at.

Usage

lake_open(uri, version = NULL, timestamp = NULL, credentials = NULL)

lake_load(tbl, version = NULL, timestamp = NULL)

lake_version(tbl)

Arguments

uri

Location of the table, the directory that holds _delta_log/: a local path, or an Azure URI in one of the forms of the Azure section.

version

Version to open, a whole number. NULL, the default, is the latest version.

timestamp

Open the latest version committed at or before this time, a POSIXct. The commit time is the commit's in-commit timestamp when the table records them, and the commit file's modification time otherwise, made increasing as lake_versions() describes. A time before the first commit opens the first version; a log with no commit file (checkpoints alone) has no commit times, and is a zulake_error_version. Give version or timestamp, not both.

credentials

A function of no arguments returning a bearer token for Azure Storage, as a string (see the Azure section), or NULL for anonymous requests. Not used for local paths.

tbl

A snapshot, from lake_open() or lake_load().

Value

lake_open() and lake_load() return a snapshot, an object of class zulake_table. lake_version() returns the version a snapshot holds, a whole number as a double.

Every error is a condition of class zulake_error, with a subclass that says why: zulake_error_argument (an argument of the wrong type or value, such as a version that is not a whole number), zulake_error_not_table (no Delta log at uri), zulake_error_version (no such version, or one no longer in the log), zulake_error_uri (a URI zulake cannot open), zulake_error_storage (a file that cannot be read, or a log file whose size is not the one its listing gives; from Azure with the HTTP status and Azure's error code), zulake_error_auth (credentials refused), zulake_error_corrupt_log (a log that breaks the protocol, such as a commit that is not JSON, a line holding two actions, a partition value of the wrong type, a schema with a type the protocol does not define or two fields of one name, or a _last_checkpoint naming a checkpoint the log does not hold whole), zulake_error_checkpoint_unreadable (its checkpoint field gives the version, parent the read failure) and zulake_error_unsupported_feature, whose feature field names the feature (also for a timestamp_ntz or variant column whose reader feature the protocol does not declare).

Details

The snapshot holds the version's protocol, metadata, live files, tombstones, application transactions and metadata domains. It is checked before it is returned: a table that needs a reader feature zulake does not support is refused with an error naming that feature, before any data file is read, because ignoring a feature returns wrong rows.

zulake reads tables on local disk and on Azure (Blob Storage and Data Lake Storage Gen2), replaying the log from the latest checkpoint at or before the version (classic, multi-part or V2, with its sidecars), or from the first commit when there is none. A checkpoint that cannot be read is passed over for an earlier one or for the commits; a version that needs it, in a log that no longer reaches commit 0, is refused with a zulake_error_checkpoint_unreadable error. A version whose commits were cleaned up, older than the earliest checkpoint, is a zulake_error_version error. A file's dataChange from a checkpoint is the checkpoint's copy, which some writers set to FALSE.

Azure

A table on Azure is given by one of three URI forms, which all reach the same blobs through the Blob service API:

  • abfss://<container>@<account>.dfs.core.windows.net/<path>

  • https://<account>.dfs.core.windows.net/<container>/<path>

  • https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<path>

Other schemes (s3://, gs://, abfs://, http://, ...) are refused with a zulake_error_uri error, and so is a URI with a query string, such as a SAS: zulake authenticates with a bearer token only.

credentials is a function you write, which zulake calls with no arguments to get a Microsoft Entra ID access token for Azure Storage (audience https://storage.azure.com), as a string. zulake does not obtain tokens itself: return one from the Azure CLI, a managed identity or a package such as AzureAuth. It is called before the first request, and once more when Azure answers 401 (an expired token); a second 401, or a 403, is a zulake_error_auth error. The token is sent only in the Authorization header: it is not kept in the snapshot, printed, or put in any error. Without credentials, requests are anonymous, which only a public container answers.

A file the log names by an absolute Azure URI is read only when it is in the table's own account and container; one elsewhere is a zulake_error_uri error, and no request is sent there.

The snapshot does not keep credentials either; later calls on it, such as lake_read(), use it through the R session. A snapshot saved with saveRDS() and read in another session has none: open the table again.

See also

lake_is_table() to check a location first.

Examples

# The example table the package ships: orders partitioned by region, five versions.
path <- system.file("extdata", "orders", package = "zulake")
tbl <- lake_open(path)
tbl
#> <zulake_table> delta table, version 4
#> uri:       /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/zulake/extdata/orders
#> committed: 2025-01-10 09:00:00 UTC
#> files:     12 (16890 bytes)
#> records:   23
lake_version(tbl)
#> [1] 4

# An older version, by number or by the time it was committed:
lake_version(lake_open(path, version = 1))
#> [1] 1
lake_version(lake_load(tbl, timestamp = as.POSIXct("2025-01-08 12:00", tz = "UTC")))
#> [1] 2

# On Azure: a token for Azure Storage from the Azure CLI. Not run, because
# it needs an Azure account and a signed-in CLI.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
token <- function() {
  system2("az", c(
    "account", "get-access-token", "--resource", "https://storage.azure.com",
    "--query", "accessToken", "--output", "tsv"
  ), stdout = TRUE)
}
tbl <- lake_open("abfss://lake@myaccount.dfs.core.windows.net/sales", credentials = token)
lake_files(tbl)
} # }
